rounds.q: What % of a US dollar bill is cotton?
rounds.why: The rest is linen, and it takes about 4,000 double folds to tear a bill.
rounds.src: US Currency Education Program (Federal Reserve), Currency Facts (read 2026)
rounds.fun: A dollar bill is 75% cotton and the rest is linen. Fancy!

rounds.q: The US made its last everyday penny in 2025. How many years had it made them?
rounds.why: The Mint struck the last one in November 2025, and by its estimate 300 billion are still out there.
rounds.src: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, Page One Economics (May 2026); last struck Nov 12, 2025
rounds.fun: 232 years of pennies, and about 300 billion still out there. Check the couch cushions!

rounds.q: About how many cents does it cost to make one nickel?
rounds.why: It was 13.31 cents in the Mint's 2025 budget year, well over twice what the coin is worth.
rounds.src: United States Mint, 2025 Annual Report (fiscal 2025 data)
rounds.fun: A 5 cent coin that costs 13 cents to make. Keep the change!

rounds.q: How many tiny ridges run around the edge of a US quarter?
rounds.why: A dime has 118 and a half dollar has 150. Pennies and nickels have smooth edges.
rounds.fun: 119 ridges on a quarter and 118 on a dime. Run a thumbnail around one!

rounds.q: How many billion coins did the US Mint make in its 2025 budget year?
rounds.why: Pennies were 4.8 billion of the 8.0 billion coins shipped, even in their final stretch.
rounds.src: United States Mint, 2025 Annual Report (fiscal 2025 data)
rounds.fun: 8 billion coins in a year, and 4.8 billion were pennies. Clink clink!
